newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore banks say no meeting planned.
newsitem.headline: Singapore banks say no meeting planned.

text.p: The Association of Banks in Singapore (ABS) has no plans to meet on Friday to talk about the dual listing issue, a spokeswoman said.
"We have had calls asking about this meeting. But there is no meeting," she told Reuters.
Dealers said rumours of an ABS meeting started circulating in the afternoon. The rumours said the subject was the dual listing of local and foreign shares for Singapore banks.
"They say the four local banks are holding a meeting right now," said one dealer.
The local and foreign shares of DBS Bank, OCBC Bank, Overseas Union Bank and United Overseas Bank continued to see volatile trading on uncertainty over the fate of dual listings of the shares.
ABS chairman Ng Kee Choe, president of DBS Bank, was not immediately available for comment.
